lanes.source_family: Declared query set (plan A.1): wildfire/weather production shut-ins with a stated volume in Alberta, BC, Saskatchewan; opened pages from the results. No AER or
registry: Alberta and BC wildfire and shut-in reporting (AER, provincial governments, operators)
Statistics Canada tables (web API)
lanes.finding: No new event. Every volume-bearing result for 2023 and 2025 resolves to the two Alberta records already in the corpus; 2024 yields only Firebag, for which no opened page states a shut-in volume (215,000 bpd is the site's size). The AER media-centre items read (May-November 2026) contain no wildfire or shut-in announcement, and Alberta's season-end release of 2026-11-02 reports a quiet 2026 season (785 fires, under 18,000 ha) with no mention of energy impacts; neither is proof of absence. Published shut-in volumes in this lane come from operator statements relayed by wire services and from analyst tallies, not from the regulator or provincial pages opened. The declared strings cannot surface BC or Saskatchewan events; a re-run should add province-specific strings.
lanes.limitation: One declared query (2025, second string) was never run and the 2026 re-run did not happen, so search coverage of June-November 2026 rests on three fetched pages, not on queries. The authority and operator half is thin: AER's media centre was read only for May-November 2026 (3 of about 45 listing pages; 2022-2025 unread), BC Energy Regulator page 1 of 53 only, Saskatchewan's news search returned nothing relevant and was not enumerated, and Suncor (403) and Cenovus (script-only) release archives could not be read. BC and Saskatchewan shut-ins were not searched in substance: both declared strings name Alberta or the oil sands.

lanes.source_family: Per-terminal query set (plan A.1) for LNG Canada, Westridge, Canaport, RIPET, Pembina Prince Rupert, Whiffen Head; operator news pages by direct fetch.
registry: Canadian export terminal reporting (operators)
lanes.finding: The plan's bare terminal tokens do not work as search strings: "RIPET" resolves to the RIPE NCC internet registry, "Westridge" to place names, "Canaport" to general Canadian port news. Canaport was renamed Saint John LNG, and that name was not searched. Incidental, outside CL1's universe and not examined: results repeatedly showed a fire at Westshore Terminals (coal, British Columbia) on 16 Aug 2025 closing a berth for about ten weeks.
lanes.limitation: Pembina Prince Rupert had one general (variant) query and no year queries; Whiffen Head 2022 and 2023 were not run; RIPET and Canaport year queries ran as written but the bare tokens matched unrelated subjects, so those years are run-but-uninformative rather than searched in substance.
